Eleven comments

The Hen and Her Brood?

The Repeal of the Union appears on The Best of the Chieftains - I don’t know which album it originally came from. It’s a real piping tune. Those D-E-D groups in bars 1 and 4 of the first part can be played as D-crans, or the E-D can be made into an F#-E-D triplet.

I’ve never come across it under any other name before. There is quite a different tune called The Hen and Her Brood, which I posted in The Session a few months ago.

↳ Posted by CreadurMawnOrganig on February 14th, 2002.

Re: The Repeal Of The Union/ Joseph’s Fancy

The Johnstons / Mick Moloney recorded this reel, followed by Trip to Durrow, as Joseph’s Fancy back in the 60s. Tony Martin (banjo) would play this set in Mise Ceoil (Tony plus Mick Rodden, fiddle, RIP, and Mick Burke, accordion), who played at the weekend in The Clarence in Rusholme, Manchester in the 70s. Thanks for those days and the music!

↳ Posted by brailsford on July 13th, 2025.
